text:
jon: FYI support escalated a customer complaining about p95/p99 regressions on the hosted text-generation route this morning. they also saw intermittent 401s while we were reproing — raising here to correlate with batcher changes.
ria: linking the support thread: https://support.example/ticket/8421 — customer observed spikes around 08:12–08:25 UTC and again ~09:05. reported model: redwood-v1-small, route: /v1/generate
oncall-bot: [ALERT] high_tail_latency continuous-batcher-service env=prod region=us-west1 metric=p99 latency=1.3s threshold=1.0s time=2026-03-15T08:13:10Z
morgan: saw the same alert — dashboards show p50 ~120ms, p95 ~280ms normally. spike p99 jumped to ~1.2s for several minutes. interestingly per-token compute is fine, token throughput isn't dropping.
samir: possible cause: continuous-batcher hold/grace window misconfig after last config rollout. small-prompt workloads can cause long-lived tiny batches, increasing tail when a late request holds a batch open.
ria: support noted "auth failed" around the same time — they pasted this error from their app: `{\"error\":\"unauthorized\",\"detail\":\"token expired\"}`. might be independent but could be concurrent retries increasing arrival jitter.
jon: timeline I pulled: 08:10 deploy of batcher config change (grace_window_ms: 30 -> 80, hold_window_ms: 10 -> 20) rolled to 40% traffic at 08:09, full at 08:11. alerts started 08:13. rolling back to previous values at 08:27 reduced p99 back to ~320ms.
morgan: interesting, increasing grace_window should reduce cost by batching more, but on skewed arrival it increases risk of a straggler keeping batch open and inflating tail. we've seen this tradeoff before.
samir: reproducer steps I used in lab to mimic customer: run 300 qps of tiny prompts (avg tokens 6) with poisson arrival and occasional auth 401 causing client-side retry (3 retries, backoff jitter). this produced p99 ~1.1s within 2 minutes using new windows.
ria: can you paste the repro harness command?
samir: sure:
```
# simplified repro
python loadgen.py --qps 300 --prompt-size 6 --model redwood-v1-small \
  --arrival=poisson --client-retries='3,rand(0.1,0.8)' --route /v1/generate
```
and batcher config snippet we tested:
```
continuous_batcher:
  grace_window_ms: 80
  hold_window_ms: 20
  max_batch_size: 64
```
jon: logs from prod around 08:14 (stripped):
```
[08:14:05] continuous-batcher: opened batch id=abc123 size=3 hold_for=80ms
[08:14:05] request: tenant=acme token=xxx status=200
[08:14:05.077] request: tenant=acme token=expired status=401 retrying
[08:14:05.400] continuous-batcher: flushed batch id=abc123 size=3 latency=1.12s
```
ria: so the expired token caused a retry that arrived late and extended the batch life? the `flushed ... latency=1.12s` line shows the hold combined with retry jitter.
morgan: mitigation we applied: temporarily reduced grace_window_ms to 20 and set max_batch_size to 32 for high-traffic routes at 08:27; that brought p99 down quickly. also enabled a short per-tenant tail-shed policy — if a request causes an auth failure we don't hold the batch waiting for retries.
samir: longer-term fix ideas:
- make batcher aware of auth-layer retry patterns (if upstream reports 401, don't extend hold)
- introduce an adaptive grace window: shrink when arrival variance high
- implement per-request "no-wait" flag for known low-latency SLAs
jon: also note billing system saw elevated request counts due to retries — support flagged an invoice spike. support: customer asked for a billing credit; we should correlate the retry storm with their invoice.
support: I filed a credit request and flagged finance with the customer ticket. I've attached the raw request IDs.
ria: next steps for eng-sre:
1) add a short-term automation to rollback grace_window when p99 > 800ms for 5m on a route
2) add a telemetry tag when retries are auth-fail so we can detect correlation (instrumentation ticket created)
3) finalize adaptive grace window RFC (assign owners)
jon: I'm putting a quick runbook update under /runbooks/continuous-batcher-latency.md with the rollback commands and repro steps.
morgan: can someone own the instrumentation ticket? samir?
samir: I'll take it and put up a draft next week. will also add the loadgen snippet to the test harness so QA can run it before rolling config.
jon: thanks all. closing loop with support: reply to customer with explanation + temporary credit while we harden. :thumbsup:
support: replied to customer with mitigation summary and ETA for a permanent fix. they appreciated the quick turnaround. :eyes:
